findings.excerpt:
theorem finite_cost_branchCoupling
    {nu : Measure E3} [IsProbabilityMeasure nu] {K : Set E3} (hK : IsCompact K)
findings.problem: Probability normalization is stronger than necessary for finite cost. The separation argument works for arbitrary measures, and the final integral lemma requires only a finite measure.
findings.proposed_change:
Use the statement:
theorem finite_cost_branchCoupling
    {nu : Measure E3} [IsFiniteMeasure nu] {K : Set E3} (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hnu : ∀ᵐ x ∂nu, x ∈ K) {H : Fin 4 → E3 → E3}
    (hH : ∀ i, Measurable (H i)) (hcont : ∀ i, ContinuousOn (H i) K)
    (hdisjoint : Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (components K H i) (components K H j))) :
    (∫⁻ t, coulombCost t ∂branchCoupling nu (H 0) (H 1) (H 2) (H 3)) < ⊤.
Replace the probability-instance step with a local IsFiniteMeasure instance for branchCoupling: unfold its definition, use Measure.isFiniteMeasure_map for its six summands, the finite-addition instance, and Measure.smul_finite for the coefficient 1 / 6. The last two proof steps remain applicable. This includes nu = 0; no division by its mass is needed.
findings.benefit: Applies directly to unnormalized finite measures, restrictions, and finite rescalings without a separate normalization argument.

findings.excerpt: (hdisjoint : Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (components K H i) (components K H j))) :
findings.problem: Full pairwise disjointness also separates components belonging to different branches, although those pairs never occur together in a triple. In particular, it excludes identical or overlapping alternative branches even when each branch is uniformly collision-free.
findings.proposed_change:
Provide the weaker core statement:
theorem exists_ae_separated_branchCoupling
    {nu : Measure E3} {K : Set E3} (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hnu : ∀ᵐ x ∂nu, x ∈ K) {H : Fin 4 → E3 → E3}
    (hH : ∀ i, Measurable (H i)) (hcont : ∀ i, ContinuousOn (H i) K)
    (hcentral : ∀ i, Disjoint K (H i '' K))
    (houter : Disjoint (H 0 '' K) (H 1 '' K) ∧
      Disjoint (H 2 '' K) (H 3 '' K)) :
    ∃ eta : ℝ, 0 < eta ∧
      ∀ᵐ t ∂branchCoupling nu (H 0) (H 1) (H 2) (H 3),
        CoulombEstimates.Separated eta t.
Apply exists_uniform_compact_separation separately to the Fin 3 families ![K, H 0 '' K, H 1 '' K] and ![K, H 2 '' K, H 3 '' K]. Their compactness follows from hK.image_of_continuousOn; the proposed hypotheses give their pairwise disjointness. Take the minimum of the two positive bounds, then use the existing ae_branchCoupling argument. Empty K is already covered by the compact-separation lemma. Retain the original statement as a corollary if needed, and expose the weaker hypotheses in the combined support/separation and finite-cost results.
findings.benefit: Supports mixtures whose alternative branches overlap, including H 0 = H 2 and H 1 = H 3, without weakening separation within either actual triple.

findings.excerpt:
have hcompact : IsCompact (⋃ i, components K H i) :=
    isCompact_iUnion (compact_components hK hcont)
findings.problem: This concentration statement requires compactness and continuity only to establish measurability of the component union. Those geometric assumptions unnecessarily exclude measurable noncompact supports and discontinuous measurable transports.
findings.proposed_change:
Generalize to:
theorem ae_mem_branchMarginal_components
    {nu : Measure E3} {K : Set E3}
    (hnu : ∀ᵐ x ∂nu, x ∈ K) {H : Fin 4 → E3 → E3}
    (hH : ∀ i, Measurable (H i))
    (hU : MeasurableSet (⋃ i, components K H i)) :
    ∀ᵐ x ∂branchMarginal nu (H 0) (H 1) (H 2) (H 3),
      x ∈ ⋃ i, components K H i.
Delete the hcompact construction and pass hU to ae_map_iff at line 78; the remaining proof is unchanged. The compact-support caller can supply the existing compact union's measurableSet proof. No measurability of individual images is silently assumed, and empty K and the zero measure remain allowed.
findings.benefit: Separates the measure-theoretic concentration fact from compact-support geometry, making it reusable for measurable unions beyond the compact continuous construction.
